A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRADIEND research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRADIEND training, gender-classification and debiasing experiments on four encoder-only models, including benchmark results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports original results for GPT-2, LLaMA, and LLaMA-Instruct, additional comparators, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The gradient-difference target, single-neuron encoder, linear decoder, and parameter-update rule remain unchanged. v2 adds a causal-model adaptation that computes gradients from prefix-only next-token prediction, with instruction prompting for LLaMA-Instruct (Section 3.1; Appendix C.2).

E1.justification: The datasets and established benchmarks are retained, but task coverage expands from masked prediction to causal completion and instruction-prompted prediction. These introduce different context availability and output requirements, including reformulated name-prediction tasks and causal profession completions (Appendices B.2, C.2, and F).

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated RLACE and LEACE baselines and four hybrids: CDA or DROPOUT combined with INLP or SENTDEBIAS. Tables 11–12 establish their participation; the original comparators and GRADIEND combinations are retained. CDA/DROPOUT variants are explicitly omitted for the new LLaMA experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds decoder-only model configurations, LLaMA-specific learning rates and validation subsampling, and perplexity evaluation on 1,000 GENeutral samples alongside retained MLM accuracy on 10,000 samples. LLaMA GLUE evaluation uses zero-shot prediction without STS-B, whereas other models are fine-tuned. Section 6.4 also introduces proportional-rank aggregation.

E4.justification: v2 extends gender-factor/learning-rate sensitivity analysis to GPT-2 and both LLaMA variants (Figures 7–9), and adds their profession-prediction case studies (Tables 21–23). These examine transfer of bias control to causal models and expose exceptions. The original encoder sensitivity results and name-split/order analysis are retained; the latter is merged into Figure 10.

E5.justification: Both versions report three GRADIEND training seeds, three-run GLUE summaries, 1,000 bootstrap samples, 95% confidence intervals, and significance based on non-overlapping intervals. v2 relocates reporting details and adds result rows without establishing a changed uncertainty procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: The original tabulated encoder results, benchmark scores, GLUE/SEAT breakdowns, and prediction examples are numerically retained. v2 adds substantial results for three causal models and six additional comparison variants. For example, its new LLaMA experiment reports SS of 69.44 for the base model and 60.03 for GRADIEND BPI + INLP (Table 12); Table 4 adds aggregate rankings.

T1.justification: Section 6.3 adds an explicit signed-update derivation yielding 2αbd, correcting v1's statement that the difference is twice be. Appendix B.1 also defines the new decoder-only score LMSDec = 1/(1 + perplexity). The underlying encoder-decoder equations and bias-index structure are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden demonstrated applicability from four encoder-only models to multiple transformer architectures, including generative models previously proposed as future work. The introduction also expands the comparison claim to competing hybrid approaches. The central targeted-feature-learning and gender-debiasing contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning hybrid-method complementarity, aggregate superiority, and a polar rather than merely binary learned feature. It adds decoder-specific qualifications: the name-overfitting probe could not be adapted reliably, and profession predictions sometimes contradict intended bias directions. The new Ethical Statement discusses deliberate bias amplification and misuse; earlier uncertainty caveats remain in Appendix D.2.

D1.justification: v2 supplies debiased checkpoint identifiers for all seven models (Table 8), causal/instruction prompts, and evaluation-harness access information. It adds GPU memory, system RAM, multi-GPU usage, and training-time disclosures. Table 7 clarifies gradient-computation batch size 32 versus GRADIEND batch size 1; this clarification alone does not establish changed training.

R1.justification: Related work adds RLACE and LEACE as INLP successors and a fairness survey, with additional GPT-2, LLaMA, and evaluation-harness citations. Detailed attention-head and movement-pruning discussions are removed. The principal positioning against unsupervised sparse-autoencoder feature discovery remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The central comparison narrative is rewritten around aggregate ranks, with detailed results and uncertainty discussion reorganized into Appendix D.2. Related-work subsections are reordered, training/convergence material is regrouped, and an Ethical Statement replaces the Impact Statement. Terminology is revised throughout to accommodate token prediction and polar features.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Heatmaps are rearranged, Figure 2 is expanded, and new sensitivity figures and tables are added. A new aggregate Table 4 replaces the main-text raw comparison, which survives in expanded appendix tables. The two original overfitting figures are combined into Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The causal-model evaluations, stronger baseline and hybrid comparisons, and expanded reproducibility information make v2 better supported and more useful. However, its new Table 4 describes cross-model language-score summaries while reproducing BERTbase entries: the reported +0.81 LMS change for GRADIEND BPI + INLP contrasts with approximately −0.61 averaged across the seven within-model changes in Tables 11–12. The detailed evidence remains available, but this reporting error limits the overall gain by weakening the main summary of capability preservation.
